concerns.location: Phase 1 Preprocessing (lines 1‑4 of the Phase Breakdown table)
concerns.text: Phenology metrics are derived from raw eBird observations without any adjustment for observer effort or sampling bias (e.g., variation in checklist duration, number of observers, or spatial heterogeneity of effort). This can confound the relationship between climate variables and phenology, violating construct validity.

Power analysis is performed post‑hoc after the data are collected. An a priori power calculation (or minimum detectable effect size planning) is missing, so the study may proceed without guaranteeing sufficient sample size to detect the targeted 0.15 day/°C effect.

The GAMM includes random intercepts and slopes but does not model temporal autocorrelation (e.g., year‑to‑year correlation) in the residuals. Ignoring temporal dependence can inflate Type I error rates for climate‑phenology associations.

The plan mentions a “permutation‑based FDR‑corrected hypothesis testing” for GAMM coefficients but does not specify how permutations preserve the hierarchical and spatial structure of the data. An improperly designed permutation scheme could yield invalid p‑values.

The plan states it will download the *full* eBird Basic Dataset (≈ 10 GB) and PRISM climate layers, storing them under `data/raw/`. The GitHub Actions free‑tier runner provides only ~14 GB of disk space, which must also accommodate intermediate files, provenance logs, and output artifacts. This exceeds the available storage and will cause the pipeline to fail before any analysis runs. Either down‑sample the eBird data to a size that fits within the runner’s disk quota or redesign the workflow to stream directly from the source without persisting the full raw files.

The implementation plan does not reference any of the contract schemas (e.g., `dataset.schema.yaml`, `phenology_metric.schema.yaml`, `gamm_results.schema.yaml`, `trajectory.schema.yaml`). According to the cross‑doc consistency rule, each contract should be exercised by at least one plan element (e.g., validation of downloaded data against `dataset.schema.yaml` or schema‑checking of model outputs against `gamm_results.schema.yaml`). Add explicit steps that validate inputs/outputs against the defined contracts.

The permutation test for route‑shift significance (Section 3.3 in research.md) shuffles yearly labels assuming independence between years. Because migration routes exhibit temporal autocorrelation, this violates the exchangeability assumption of the permutation test and may inflate Type I error. The plan should incorporate a temporally‑aware permutation scheme (e.g., block permutation) or use the same block‑bootstrap framework for hypothesis testing.
